articles.title: Cardiologist Urges Earlier ECG Screening for At-Risk Patients as India's Heart Disease Burden Grows
articles.excerpt: Dr. Vijay D'Silva says skipping early ECG screening costs lives — but U.S. guidelines add an important caveat: screening pays off for at-risk patients, not healthy low-risk adults.
articles.image_caption: An illustration shows a human heart with blood vessels over an electrocardiogram waveform. Dr. Vijay D'Silva argues early ECG screening can catch silent heart disease before symptoms appear.
articles.nri_angle: South Asians develop coronary artery disease at younger ages, so the diaspora with family history of early heart disease should raise ECG screening at their annual physical.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Your Daily Walk Alone Won't Build Fitness: Intensity, Variety, Strength Training Matter
articles.excerpt: Fitness expert Sumit Dubey says most walkers stall because comfortable-pace strolls never push the heart and lungs — faster intervals, varied routes, and strength work close the gap.
articles.image_caption: A woman walks up an outdoor stone staircase in a narrow street. Fitness coach Sumit Dubey says adding intensity and variety to daily walks is the key to improving cardiovascular fitness.
articles.nri_angle: For NRIs rooted in walking culture, the coach's advice translates to layering intensity bursts and two weekly resistance sessions onto the familiar daily walk.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Cardiologist's Three Longevity Habits: Lp(a) Test, Strength Training, Treated Sleep Apnea
articles.excerpt: Interventional cardiologist Dr. Sanjay Bhojraj says three underused steps — a one-time Lp(a) blood test, training for functional strength, and treating sleep apnea — can meaningfully slow how fast your heart ages.
articles.image_caption: A seated cable row exercise. Cardiologist Dr. Sanjay Bhojraj lists strength training among his three longevity habits, alongside an Lp(a) test and treating sleep apnea.
articles.nri_angle: South Asians carry elevated lipoprotein(a) more often than many populations, making the once-in-a-lifetime Lp(a) test the 2026 ACC/AHA guideline now recommends especially relevant for the Indian diaspora.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Drooping smile, weak arms: neurologists flag stroke warning signs in young adults
articles.excerpt: A drooping smile, a weak arm and slurred speech are the classic red flags — and with four in ten Indian stroke patients now under 50, neurologists say young adults should learn the BEFAST checklist and act within the golden hours.
articles.image_caption: Brain scans. Neurologists warn that a drooping smile, weak arms, and slurred speech can signal a stroke.

sources.label: Passionate in Marketing / World Stroke Day

articles.nri_angle: South Asians develop cardiovascular risk factors earlier and at higher rates, making BEFAST stroke awareness especially relevant in NRI households — and for spotting warning signs in ageing parents back home.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Inside Krystle D'Souza's Mumbai Home: Parisian Chic, a Glam Room and Sabyasachi Walls
articles.excerpt: The Traitors season 2 winner gave Farah Khan a tour of her self-designed Lokhandwala apartment — from a ₹35,000-a-roll Sabyasachi bedroom wall to a bedroom-sized vanity room.
articles.image_caption: Television actor Krystle D'Souza. A new feature tours her Mumbai home, from its Parisian-chic interiors to a glam room and Sabyasachi-clad walls.

gallery_images.caption: The dining and living areas of Krystle D'Souza's Lokhandwala apartment, with beige tones, wooden textures and fluted panelling. Photo: Hindustan Times.
Farah Khan with Krystle D'Souza and her cook Dilip inside the Mumbai apartment during the September 7 home-tour vlog. Photo: Farah Khan/YouTube.

articles.nri_angle: For design-minded NRIs, the tour offers a template — Parisian detailing, Sabyasachi accents and a dedicated vanity space that translate well to diaspora homes.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Paying Extra for A2 Ghee? Cardiologist Says the Label Is a Fad
articles.excerpt: Dr. Darshan Banker and the IFBA's Deepak Jolly say the A1/A2 protein distinction is irrelevant in ghee, which is 99.9% fat — portion size and verified purity matter far more.
articles.image_caption: A bowl of homemade ghee in Maharashtra. A cardiologist says the premium A2 ghee label is more marketing fad than medicine.
articles.nri_angle: A2 ghee sells at double or triple the price in diaspora grocery stores on imported health claims that these experts say don't survive scrutiny.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: How PCOS, Obesity and Insulin Resistance Lock Women in a Vicious Cycle
articles.excerpt: About two-thirds of women with PCOS have insulin resistance — and each side of the triangle intensifies the other two. Doctors say treating the condition as a metabolic disorder, not just a fertility problem, is the way out.
articles.nri_angle: PCOS runs high among Indian women and the diaspora, and South Asians develop insulin resistance at lower body weights, making early metabolic screening — not just fertility treatment — especially urgent.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: DNA Hairpin Treatment Cuts Bad Cholesterol Nearly 50% Without Statins
articles.excerpt: Scientists in Spain and the United States built short DNA molecules that switch off a cholesterol-regulating gene, cutting blood cholesterol 47% in mice after a single injection — with none of the side effects linked to statins.
articles.image_caption: A researcher at the National Human Genome Research Institute pipettes DNA from a micro test tube. Scientists used DNA-based polypurine hairpins to block production of the PCSK9 protein, cutting LDL cholesterol nearly 50% in a new study.
articles.nri_angle: South Asians face disproportionately high rates of premature heart disease, so a cheaper, non-statin cholesterol treatment could matter greatly for the diaspora if it survives clinical testing.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Myntra Tech Threads 2026: Where AI, Velocity and Indian Fashion Collide
articles.excerpt: At its Bengaluru conclave, Myntra pitched conversational discovery, creator-led shopping and an AI brand stack — arguing Indian fashion is now built in real time, not handed down from runways.
articles.image_caption: The Myntra Tech Threads 2026 branding with its 'Where Velocity Meets Voice' tagline. The showcase brings together AI, technology and Indian fashion.
articles.nri_angle: Ethnicwear was a strong awards and runway strand (Biba, House of Pataudi, Taavi) — contemporary Indian occasion wear the diaspora increasingly shops; the honoured homegrown D2C labels are ones diaspora readers seek out.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Sadhguru on Amavasya: Why Tonight's New Moon Is Spiritually Significant
articles.excerpt: September's Amavasya tithi runs tonight into tomorrow morning. Sadhguru explains why the moon's absence makes its presence more powerful — and why the new moon suits the hardworking and tough.
articles.image_caption: Sadhguru sits with folded hands against a dark night sky with the moon visible. He teaches that on Amavasya, the new moon night, the moon's absence makes its presence felt more powerfully.
articles.nri_angle: Strong fit for the site's Spirituality and Daily Wisdom readership — timely tonight, evergreen Sadhguru content, with Isha's large US and UK diaspora following.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Former SBI Manager Quits Over Burnout, Opens Yoga Studio in UP
articles.excerpt: A woman working as an assistant manager at the State Bank of India has quit her job, citing constant stress and mental exhaustion, and opened her own yoga studio in Uttar Pradesh — a story picked up by five national outlets that has become one of the week's most-shared conversations about work and wellbeing.
articles.nri_angle: Indian professionals abroad — where banking, consulting and tech jobs carry the same grind — are having the same conversation about burnout and exit plans; this story lands because the trade-off between a secure job and mental health translates across borders.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Fortis and Takeda Launch 'Mission Dengue Free India' Awareness Campaign
articles.excerpt: The nationwide initiative pairs physician-led community sessions with digital outreach to tackle a disease that officially struck over 113,000 Indians in 2025.
articles.image_caption: A mosquito feeds on human skin. Fortis Healthcare and Takeda have launched a ‘Mission Dengue Free India’ awareness campaign as mosquito-borne infections rise.
articles.nri_angle: Dengue season overlaps with the winter NRI travel window to India; the campaign's prevention guidance is directly relevant to diaspora visitors and their families.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Start Cholesterol Tests at 17, Not 40: Dr. Devi Shetty's Warning to Indians
articles.excerpt: India's leading cardiac surgeon calls for aggressive early screening as data shows nearly 9 in 10 Indian adults have abnormal cholesterol levels, with heart disease striking a decade earlier than in Western populations.
articles.image_caption: Cardiac surgeon Dr. Devi Shetty, founder of Narayana Health. He has urged Indians to begin cholesterol testing at age 17 rather than waiting until 40.
articles.nri_angle: South Asian Heart Center data and screening recommendations specific to Indian Americans and NRIs; population-specific cardiac risk markers that standard US panels miss.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Marks Eye Donation Fortnight With Two Million Still Facing Corneal Blindness
articles.excerpt: LVPEI's eye bank network has collected over 170,000 corneas since 1989, but India still performs only a fraction of the transplants it needs each year.
articles.image_caption: A close-up of a human eye. India marks Eye Donation Fortnight from August 25 to September 8 each year to raise awareness about corneal blindness affecting over two million people.
articles.nri_angle: NRIs can pledge eyes through consulates, fund eye bank expansion, and encourage family conversations about corneal donation in India.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Embeds Ayurveda and Yoga in Global Trade Deals as Experts Press for Standards
articles.excerpt: Three major trade agreements with the EU, Oman, and New Zealand include formal provisions for AYUSH systems, but credible evidence and regulation remain the missing pieces.
articles.image_caption: Traditional Ayurvedic herbs and preparations. India is embedding Ayurveda, Yoga, and other AYUSH systems into formal trade agreements with the EU, Oman, and New Zealand.
articles.nri_angle: The India-EU FTA's recognition of AYUSH qualifications could give diaspora communities in Europe better access to qualified Ayurveda and Yoga practitioners.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Weight-Loss Drug Prescriptions for US Children Under 12 Surge 310-Fold Since 2019
articles.excerpt: A new NYU Langone study finds 20,282 children ages 8 to 11 received GLP-1 drugs like Wegovy and Zepbound, with access disparities already emerging along income lines.
articles.nri_angle: For Indian-American parents, the study highlights rising childhood obesity rates in the US and emerging access gaps that may affect South Asian communities with elevated metabolic risks.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: What Should Kids Study in the Age of AI? The Answer Is Shifting Fast.
articles.excerpt: As nearly half of college students rethink their majors because of AI, educators and employers are converging on a new set of skills: critical thinking, adaptability, and the ability to ask better questions.
articles.image_caption: Students using an interactive whiteboard in a classroom. Experts say the rapid rise of AI is reshaping what skills children need to learn.
articles.nri_angle: Indian diaspora parents invest heavily in their children's education and career preparation; this piece speaks directly to the question of what skills matter as AI reshapes the job market.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Lippan Kaam: How Gujarat’s Ancient Mud-and-Mirror Craft Is Transforming Modern Homes
articles.excerpt: Once confined to the circular huts of Kutch, the centuries-old art of lippan — mixing clay, camel dung, and mirrors into shimmering wall panels — is finding a new audience among urban homeowners and interior designers worldwide.
articles.image_caption: Lippan kaam mud-and-mirror artwork in a modern home interior. The ancient Gujarati craft is finding its way into contemporary luxury homes.
articles.nri_angle: Traditional Kutchi craft gaining popularity among diaspora families as a way to bring Indian heritage into their homes abroad.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Black Sesame Seeds: 6 Health Benefits of Kala Til, According to Experts
articles.excerpt: Nutrition scientists separate evidence from hype on the trending superfood that Indian kitchens have used for centuries.
articles.image_caption: Black sesame seeds, known as kala til in Hindi. The nutrient-dense seeds contain higher levels of calcium, iron, and antioxidants than their white counterparts.
articles.nri_angle: Black sesame seeds have been a staple of Indian kitchens for centuries as kala til, used in laddoos, chutneys, and Ayurvedic remedies — now Western nutrition science is catching up.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: 13 Percent of Indian Employees Face High Burnout as AI Threatens 20 Percent Job Cuts
articles.excerpt: A Great Place To Work India study of 5.7 million employees finds persistent burnout, declining discretionary effort, and growing anxiety over AI-driven workforce reductions.
articles.image_caption: Around 13 percent of Indian employees report high-level burnout, according to Great Place To Work India, as AI-driven restructuring threatens up to 20 percent of jobs.
articles.nri_angle: Indian diaspora professionals in the U.S. and globally face similar pressures around AI adoption, burnout and shifting workplace expectations.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Gets Blood Test to Detect Hidden Cancer Recurrence After Treatment
articles.excerpt: MedGenome has launched OncoTrack MRD, described as India's first indigenous blood test that can detect residual cancer at the molecular level even when scans show no visible disease.
articles.image_caption: Blood samples in a hematology laboratory. India has approved a blood test that detects minimal residual disease, helping oncologists catch hidden cancer recurrence after treatment.
articles.nri_angle: The advancement in India's precision oncology capabilities is relevant to NRIs tracking healthcare developments in India, particularly those with family members undergoing cancer treatment back home.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Your Organs Age on Their Own Schedules — And a New Study Shows They're in Sync
articles.excerpt: Scientists analyzed 25,000 organ images and found the human body ages in distinct waves, with the ovaries acting as a potential pacemaker for whole-body aging.
articles.image_caption: Scientists found that individual organs age at different rates but are more synchronized than previously thought. The study maps biological age across multiple organ systems.
articles.nri_angle: The research has broad health implications for aging populations worldwide, including South Asian communities with higher cardiovascular and metabolic disease risk factors.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: UC Berkeley Compound Cuts Weight 18% in Mice Without Suppressing Appetite
articles.excerpt: An oral molecule called TOFA boosted energy expenditure and preserved muscle mass in obese mice, offering a potential complement to GLP-1 drugs like Ozempic.
articles.image_caption: A microscopic image of brown adipose tissue. UC Berkeley researchers found that an oral compound called TOFA activated brown fat and reduced body weight by 18 percent in obese mice over four weeks.
articles.nri_angle: Diabetes and metabolic syndrome prevalence is elevated in the Indian diaspora, making alternative weight-loss approaches that preserve muscle especially relevant.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: New Study Finds Creatine May Boost Strength After 45, Even Without Exercise
articles.excerpt: A 12-week trial of 64 middle-aged adults found that creatine supplementation improved lean mass and muscle strength — with modest gains observed even among those who did not work out.
articles.image_caption: Creatine monohydrate powder, the most commonly studied form of the supplement. A new 12-week trial found it improved muscle strength in adults over 45 even without exercise.
articles.nri_angle: Creatine's potential to preserve muscle health in midlife is relevant to aging Indian-Americans seeking accessible, evidence-based supplements.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Drug-Resistant Infections Kill Up to Half of ICU Patients in Indian Hospitals, Landmark ICMR Study Finds
articles.excerpt: A three-year study of 159,336 patients across 20 hospitals reveals that carbapenem-resistant bacteria drive sharply higher mortality and treatment costs, with most infections acquired inside healthcare facilities.
articles.image_caption: A visualization of antimicrobial-resistant bacteria. A landmark ICMR study found that drug-resistant infections kill up to half of ICU patients in Indian hospitals.
articles.nri_angle: NRIs seeking hospital care in India should be aware of antimicrobial resistance risks, particularly in ICU settings, and ask about infection-control protocols.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Jharkhand Sounds State-Wide Swine Flu Alert After Eight H1N1 Cases Confirmed
articles.excerpt: The state has ordered hospitals to reserve dedicated beds and deployed surveillance at airports and railway stations as seasonal influenza cases rise across India.
articles.image_caption: A colorized transmission electron micrograph of the H1N1 influenza virus. Jharkhand issued a state-wide alert after eight cases of swine flu were confirmed.
articles.nri_angle: NRIs planning travel to eastern India during the festive season should be aware of the H1N1 alert and follow standard influenza precautions.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Prostate Cancer Cases Rise 3% Annually as Updated Guidelines Push Earlier Screening
articles.excerpt: The American Cancer Society estimates 333,830 new U.S. diagnoses in 2026, while updated AUA/SUO guidelines lower the recommended screening age and introduce flexible intervals.
articles.image_caption: Dr. Daniel W. Lin, chair of the American Urological Association guideline update panel. Updated screening recommendations now emphasize life expectancy over age-based thresholds for prostate cancer testing.
articles.nri_angle: Indian-American men, particularly those over 50, should discuss personalized screening with their doctors as updated guidelines now recommend earlier and more flexible PSA testing.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The Science Behind Haldi Doodh: Why Turmeric Milk May Improve Your Sleep
articles.excerpt: The ancient Indian drink combines anti-inflammatory curcumin with calming spices, and modern research is beginning to validate what generations of Indian families already knew.
articles.image_caption: A glass of haldi doodh, the traditional Indian turmeric milk drink. Research suggests the curcumin in turmeric may help improve sleep quality by modulating brain chemistry.
articles.nri_angle: Haldi doodh is a cherished Indian tradition that diaspora families continue to practise, now supported by growing scientific evidence for its health benefits.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Rahul Roy Opens Up About Speech Recovery Six Years After Brain Stroke
articles.excerpt: The Aashiqui actor says he takes eight medicines daily and has switched to a vegan diet since suffering a cerebrovascular stroke in 2020.
articles.nri_angle: Rahul Roy's recovery story resonates with Indian diaspora families familiar with the Aashiqui-era actor and the realities of stroke rehabilitation.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk
